solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Everyone's turned up with a full picnic

definitions.meaning: when everyone has turned up, every person is present and accounted for
idiom inverted: someone 'a sandwich short of a picnic' is dim, so one with a full picnic is mentally sharp

explanation.surface: Every guest has arrived and the hamper is packed to the brim.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the British phrase 'a sandwich short of a picnic', meaning not very bright; a full picnic means fully sane.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both that the whole group is present and, informally, that a person is shrewd and of sound mind.

clue.text: Too small? Shoe's not that large

indicators.note: 'not' tells us the letter for small is left out of the shoe

parts.note: a sandal is an open shoe
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A worried shopper asks if a shoe is too small and is told it isn't that big.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too small?' reads as one shopping question, but 'Too' is the definition and 'small' the letter to drop; 'not' signals the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial tag phrase is used to mean 'as well' or 'also', just like the word too.

clue.text: Exercise with track-suit discarded?

definitions.meaning: a school exercise is a piece of teaching, a class or task set to learn from
read as two words, someone who has taken off a track-suit has fewer clothes on

explanation.surface: A jogger strips off the track-suit before working out.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer as LESS ON, describing a person wearing less after shedding a track-suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A school exercise is a teaching period or task, the sense a teacher sets for pupils.

clue.text: Old woman brought silver up for ritual

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'up' means the following words are read from the bottom

parts.note: 'had' can mean brought, as in had a guest round
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A crone hoists up silver for some ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought' in the sense of 'had' (had friends round) is the hard step; 'up' turns it and the silver over.
explanation.definitionFit: The Haggadah is the Jewish text recited at the Passover Seder, setting out the order of that ceremony.

clue.text: A fast runner, though no winger: what about joining the Gunners?

definitions.text: A fast runner, though no winger

indicators.note: 'joining' the Gunners is taken as getting in among them, so the turned word goes inside their letters

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners

indicators.note: 'about' signals that the word for what is turned round

parts.note: 'eh?' is an exclamation meaning what?

explanation.surface: A sprinter who isn't a football winger considers signing for Arsenal, nicknamed the Gunners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' misleads towards football; here it is a creature with working wings. The Gunners here are the Royal Artillery, not the football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird that runs very fast, so it can run but not fly.

clue.text: Cheat dropping off car key

indicators.note: 'dropping off' says the word car falls away from the cheat

parts.note: a cardsharp is a cheat at card games

explanation.surface: A swindler leaves a vehicle key behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking CAR from CARDSHARP leaves the musical key. 'key' looks like a car key but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: D sharp is a musical key, the scale built on the note a semitone above D.

clue.text: Winding Bible 2s up during round of drinks?

indicators.note: 'during' places the turned Bible lessons inside the turned word for drinks
'round of' turns the word for drinks around so it reads backwards

parts.note: a dog laps water, so laps means drinks

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'up' means the abbreviation for Bible lessons is read from the bottom

parts.note: 2 down is LESSON, so Bible lessons are RI, Religious Instruction

explanation.surface: Bible classes keep going up during a pub round, a merry scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round of drinks' looks like a pub round but turns the word for drinks back to front. '2s' refers to the answer at 2 down, so Bible 2s are Religious Instruction lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral staircase or path is a winding one, coiling round and round.

clue.text: War cries winding companies up?

indicators.note: the letters of the battle shouts are twisted, as a winding road twists, into a new order

explanation.surface: Battle shouts rouse military companies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'companies up?' is a cryptic hint: crews who are up in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircrews are the teams of people who staff aeroplanes, so they are groups working aloft.

clue.text: In row, perhaps, bad cut in first half of game

indicators.note: 'in' says the trimmed word for bad goes inside the half-game
'first half of' keeps only the opening four of the game's eight letters

parts.note: ping-pong is table tennis

indicators.note: 'cut' means the word for bad loses its final letter

parts.note: addle, of an egg, means rotten or bad

explanation.surface: Bad cuts in a game of rowing, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of the word for bad; 'in' puts what remains inside the half-game. Ping-pong bats are also called paddles, a nice touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddling propels a boat with paddles, so one doing it may be out in a row on the water.

clue.text: Stays a desire for extra cycling clash

indicators.note: 'cycling' means the letters go round, the final one coming to the front

parts.note: 'is' can mean stays, as in 'it is here'
greed is the desire for more than one needs

explanation.surface: A wish for more cycling leads to an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the D at the end of ISAGREED to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To clash with someone is to be at odds with them, holding opposing views.

clue.text: Elgar's most famous variation in D-minor?

indicators.note: a variation reworks the original notes, so the letters of the key are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about Elgar's best-known Enigma variation being written in D minor.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter of this puzzle is also called Elgar, adding to the joke. 'variation' is both the musical term and the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimrod, the ninth of Elgar's Enigma Variations, is his best-known piece of music.

clue.text: Gun clip

definitions.meaning: a short-barrelled revolver of the late 1800s
a ... clip is a strong spring clip for holding papers

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are short for longer names: the British Bull Dog revolver and the spring clip for papers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a stubby pocket revolver and a stationery clamp.

clue.text: Female I see after toilet scrubber

indicators.note: 'after' places the woman and the exclamation after the toilet

parts.note: loo is a British word for toilet
'ah' is an exclamation of understanding, I see

explanation.surface: A woman notices something beside a toilet brush.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is the dried fibrous gourd used as a bath sponge for scrubbing the skin.

clue.text: Under those responsible for hearing usual suspect must gather broken bits of bar

indicators.note: suspect is read as an adjective, dubious, so the letters of usual are not to be trusted in their order
'broken bits of' says the letters of bar are split up and scattered among the others

explanation.surface: A police scene: the usual suspect has picked up shards of a smashed bar.
explanation.walkthrough: USUAL is rearranged with B, A and R broken apart inside it. 'Those responsible for hearing' are the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Sub- means below and aural concerns the ears, so the word means situated below the ears.

clue.text: Lifted note about Polish farm-workers

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'Lifted' raises the string so it reads from the bottom
'about' says the abbreviation for note goes round the word for polish

parts.note: NB, nota bene, means note well
to emery is to polish with emery paper

explanation.surface: A raised note about a Polish farmhand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives N-EMERY-B, which 'Lifted' reverses. 'Polish' poses as the nationality but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A byre is a cowshed, so byremen are farmhands who tend the cattle.

clue.text: Perhaps deserting allegedly badly-behaved old Father of the House

indicators.note: behaving badly suggests the letters of allegedly run riot into a new order
'deserting' tells us the letters for perhaps are left behind from the mix

parts.note: e.g., for example, is a way of saying perhaps

explanation.surface: An elderly senior MP is accused of misbehaving and desertion.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLEGEDLY loses E and G and the rest is rearranged. Father of the House is the title of the longest-serving MP in the UK House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Tam Dalyell, Labour MP 1962 to 2005, held the title of longest-serving member in his final parliament.

clue.text: Feel obligation to knight War Poet

parts.note: to owe someone is to be in their debt
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A sense of duty towards a knighted soldier-poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilfred Owen is the best known of the First World War poets, killed in 1918.

clue.text: Wants to live around a watery Eurasian expanse

indicators.note: 'around' places the verb for live round the word for wants

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live
lacks means wants, is without

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to settle near a broad body of water between Europe and Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Sea is the inland sea bordered by Ukraine, Russia, Turkey and other Eurasian countries.

clue.text: Old horse base now divides work

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms

indicators.note: 'divides' says the word for now splits the work in two

parts.note: an opus is a work, especially of music
hip means fashionable, now

explanation.surface: An aged horse's stable is split by current work.
explanation.definitionFit: Eohippus is the small prehistoric ancestor of the horse, living about 50 million years ago.

clue.text: Model husband home raising family

parts.note: man is used for a husband, as in man and wife

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'raising' lifts the word for home so it reads upwards

parts.note: 'in' means at home
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A model husband at home bringing up a family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' looks like bringing up children, but turns IN over to NI.
explanation.definitionFit: A mannikin is a dummy figure, such as a tailor's or artist's model of the body.

clue.text: Ladies and Gentlemen Prefer Blondes, in my book

definitions.meaning: public toilets labelled Ladies and Gentlemen, in British slang

definitions.text: Gentlemen Prefer Blondes, in my book
definitions.meaning: the 1925 novel's author, Anita, would call it 'my book'

explanation.surface: An announcer's greeting turns into a book reviewer's opinion about blondes.
explanation.walkthrough: Gentlemen serves both readings: the toilet signs, and the novel by Anita Loos.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for public toilets and the surname of the American novelist who wrote that book.

clue.text: Novelist OK with a cue, flamboyantly potting first of reds

indicators.note: in snooker potting a ball sends it in, so the red's letter goes inside
a flamboyant shot is showy and wild, so these letters are thrown into a new order
'first of' takes only the opening letter of reds

explanation.surface: A snooker player waves the cue flashily while sinking a red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potting' is snooker for sinking a ball, here putting the first letter of 'reds' inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Kerouac was the American writer of the Beat Generation novel On the Road.

clue.text: 'More just do right' the compiler admitted

indicators.note: 'admitted' lets the setter in, inside the word for do

parts.note: to fare is to do, as in how did you fare?
the compiler, the setter, refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: A setter is quoted demanding fairer treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairer is the comparative of fair, meaning even-handed, more equitable.

clue.text: Might stag go on one knee?

definitions.meaning: a stag party might go on a drinking binge
a knee is a joint that flexes the leg

explanation.walkthrough: 'go on one knee' suggests a marriage proposal before a stag night, but the clue splits after 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a wild drinking spree and, literally, a thing that bends, as the knee joint does.

clue.text: Mole's sensitive area under discussion

indicators.note: something under discussion is being spoken about, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: the groin is a tender part of the body

explanation.surface: Someone's delicate body part, perhaps a mole on it, being talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' tempts towards the animal or a skin blemish but is a sea wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a breakwater, and a groyne is a low wall built out into the sea to check erosion.

clue.text: Leaves prepared for refreshing cha-cha, buckling in?

indicators.note: buckling in a passenger straps them inside a seat, so the little word goes inside

parts.note: cha is a colloquial word for tea, taken as written here
taken as written
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Dancers stop for a reviving drink, belting in for a cha-cha.
explanation.walkthrough: The dance 'cha-cha' is really two separate words for tea, each used differently; 'buckling' belts the small word inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: China tea is tea grown in China, whose leaves are brewed for a refreshing drink.

clue.text: Win over the last one listening?

parts.note: the end is the last part
an ear is what listens

explanation.surface: Winning over the final listener in an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear oneself to someone is to make them fond of you, to charm them.

clue.text: End of bout nothing to talk about

indicators.note: 'about' says the string is turned round

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to yak is to chatter

explanation.surface: There is nothing to say about the end of a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockout, written KO and spelt out in boxing slang, ends a boxing match.

clue.text: Fine football game boycotted by Member of Parliament

indicators.note: a boycott means staying away, so the bird drops out of the game

parts.note: the Super Bowl is the American football championship game
a group of owls is called a parliament, so an owl is a member

explanation.surface: An MP refuses to attend a big football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member of Parliament' looks like an MP, but means a member of a parliament of owls.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb means excellent, of very fine quality.

clue.text: Unfortunately dated leap years certainly don't!

definitions.meaning: an archaic cry of regret, an old-fashioned 'alas'
split 4,1,3, leap years with 29 February never fall a day short

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as LACK A DAY: leap years have an extra day, not a missing one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old exclamation of sorrow, used like 'alas', now archaic.

clue.text: Take in the world of a naval type?

definitions.text: the world of a naval type?
definitions.meaning: split 2,1,3: an AB, able seaman, and his orb, world

explanation.walkthrough: AB is the abbreviation for an able seaman; orb means globe, so AB'S ORB is the sailor's world.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb is to soak up or assimilate, as a sponge soaks up water.

clue.text: Chocolatiers have large plant by western side of racecourse

indicators.note: in an across entry the western side is the left end, the opening letter

parts.note: to own is to have
a tree is a large plant

explanation.surface: Chocolate makers own a big tree beside the west of a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just means beside, and the racecourse letter comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowntree's was a famous York confectionery firm, makers of Kit Kat and other chocolate bars.
